original_question: Suppose (X, d) is a uniformly discrete non-separable metric space. Must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be non-normal?
target_in_paper: Question 2.5 in Section 2, “The Normality Problem and Associated Questions”: “Let (X,d) be a uniformly discrete and non-separable metric space. Must (2^X,T_W(d)) be non-normal?” This is the paper’s exact narrow formulation corresponding to your draft, rather than the broader conjecture discussed just before it. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper-faithful statement: it has the right hypotheses (uniformly discrete, non-separable metric space), the right hyperspace/topology notation ((2^X,T_W(d))), and it asks about non-normality of the whole Wijsman hyperspace. It also does not add extra assumptions that are absent from the paper. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
missing_details: State explicitly that 2^X denotes the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X; otherwise 2^X can be misread as the full powerset. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

Define T_W(d) explicitly: it is the Wijsman topology on 2^X, equivalently the weakest topology making each map A ↦ d(x,A) continuous for x∈X, where d(x,A)=inf{d(x,a):a∈A}. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

For a fully stand-alone question, unpack “uniformly discrete” in the standard metric sense as: there exists ε>0 such that d(x,y)≥ε for all distinct x,y∈X; this is the notion the surrounding paragraph motivates via an ε-discrete subspace Y. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

The nearby context should be kept in mind: the paper distinguishes the whole hyperspace from the punctured subspace 2^X\{X}; Proposition 2.6 and Theorem 2.7 explain why Question 2.5 is specifically about whole-space normality. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
refined_question: Let (X,d) be a non-separable uniformly discrete metric space, meaning that there exists ε>0 such that d(x,y)≥ε whenever x≠y. Let 2^X denote the set of all non-empty closed subsets of X, endowed with the Wijsman topology T_W(d), i.e. the topology of pointwise convergence of the distance maps A ↦ d(x,A)=inf{d(x,a):a∈A} for x∈X. Must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X,T_W(d)) be a non-normal topological space? ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
justification: The draft is capturing Question 2.5, not the broader conjecture stated after Problem 2.2. The paper first recalls the general conjectural picture for normality, then observes that every non-separable metric space contains an ε-discrete subspace Y of size ℵ1 and that 2^Y is a closed subspace of (2^X,T_W(d)); this is exactly the motivation given before Question 2.5. The nearby results then sharpen the context without changing the target: Proposition 2.6 shows that 2^X\{X} contains a closed copy of ω1×(ω1+1), and Theorem 2.7 gives an equivalence involving normality of 2^X\{X}, not of the whole hyperspace. So the unresolved paper-faithful question matching your draft is precisely whether the entire Wijsman hyperspace must be non-normal in the uniformly discrete non-separable case. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
